rows.why: The part of S1 that a ticket would leave open is the task's status after the first partial release. Item 10 asks exactly that, and its pick, "partially released" while a balance remains, matches. Item 2 asks about the unit of the share, not the release outcome, so it fits less well.

Item 1 asks how an uneven share is rounded. The pick rounds down with BigInt integer division, which gives 749 and stays exact up to MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. The leftover goes to the UAT release, giving 250, so the two add up to the bounty.
Item 8 asks how much UAT approval releases. The pick releases the bounty minus all earlier releases, which is the remaining balance S3 expects.
Item 7 asks what a failed hidden-test run does and whether anything is saved. The pick returns the current state without saving, so nothing is recorded and the task stays locked.
Item 5 asks what happens when UAT is approved before the hidden tests pass. The pick rejects the event with an error and records nothing, as S5 expects.
Item 9 asks what a zero bounty does. The pick sets "pro bono" but still records releases of 0 for both events. S6 says no release is ever recorded.

Item 6 asks what a repeated event does. The pick ignores repeats by release kind, not event id, and saves nothing. That covers both the same id "e1" and a different event of the same kind, as S7 requires.

Item 11 asks how overlapping events are handled. The pick runs events one at a time through a promise queue, so the second copy sees the release already made and records nothing. Exactly one release results, whether the ids match or not.

Item 11 also asks whether an error blocks later events. The pick rejects only the failed event's own caller and does not block later events, so a retry after a failed save goes through. Item 7 is about a failed test run, not a failed save.
